description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/README.md:54-116

CURRENT BLOCK (excerpt):
    \`\`\`rust
    pub trait ContactsBackend: JmapBackend {
        /// Create a new AddressBook or ContactCard.
        fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
            &self,
            account_id: &Id,
            create_id: &str,
            obj: O,
        ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;
        ...
    }
    \`\`\`

ACTUAL SHAPE (crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs:42-49):
    fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,     // ← present in source, absent in README
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        create_id: &str,
        obj: O,
    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<(Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

EVERY METHOD IN THE README TRAIT BLOCK IS MISSING `caller`:
- create_object (README:66 vs source:42)
- update_object (README:77 vs source:59)
- destroy_object (README:85 vs source:68)
- copy_contact_card (README:99 vs source:87)
- address_book_has_contents (README:110 vs source:105)

PROBLEM:
The README is stale relative to the source. The CallerCtx threading
landed in commit 514352c ("feat(server)!: thread CallerCtx through
JmapBackend trait family") on 2026-05-* — a workspace-wide change.
The README was not updated as part of that sweep.

The README is what consumers read on docs.rs and crates.io. A reader
who:
1. Reads the README and writes `fn create_object(&self, account_id:
   &Id, create_id: &str, obj: O) -> ...` will get a compile error
   ("method missing parameter").
2. Reads the README and concludes ContactsBackend does NOT receive a
   caller context will make architectural decisions on that false
   premise (e.g., "I'll thread auth context through a thread-local
   instead").

The README §"CallerCtx" section at lines 202-222 DOES describe the
mechanism correctly ("forwards `caller: &B::CallerCtx` into every
ContactsBackend ... method call"), so the documentation is internally
inconsistent: the prose says caller is threaded, the trait block says
it isn't.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That the trait signatures in the README match the trait source.
- That the README and the prose-level "CallerCtx" description are
  consistent.

RECOMMENDED:
Update README.md:54-116 to match crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs
verbatim — add `caller: &Self::CallerCtx` as the FIRST parameter on
every method. Make it a doctest-friendly block (`# use ...`-prefixed)
that compiles under `cargo test --doc`, so stale prose drift becomes a
CI failure rather than a release-time discovery.

P1 because (a) this is the primary trait-contract documentation and
(b) the contradiction with the prose-level CallerCtx section will
mislead new consumers definitively.
